summary: Backend-only iteration 19: verified (1) Emergent Object-Storage migration for the 4 file-upload endpoints — POST /api/upload/photo and POST /api/schools/{id}/signatures/upload return /api/uploads/{filename} URLs, the served bytes exactly equal the uploaded bytes with correct image/png content-type, and db.uploads records now carry a storage_path field pointing at object storage (legacy disk fallback still supported by GET /api/uploads/{filename}); (2) tenant-scoped download authorization is intact — no-token GET -> 401, cross-tenant non-superuser (SUNF admin reading MHPS file) -> 403, superuser (JTECH) -> 200 across tenants; (3) write_audit() coverage on 10 newly-instrumented mutating endpoints (create user, reset credentials, mark attendance, bulk attendance, social-skills, teacher-comment, admission POST/PUT/DELETE, academic-year toggle, report-template PUT) — every action produced a matching row via GET /api/audit-logs; (4) regression: MHPS admin GETs on /students, /users, /classes, /attendance, /gradebook all 200; (5) forgot-password (POST /api/auth/forgot-password) still returns 200 with delivery status and writes a password_reset audit row, and returns 200 for unknown username (no enumeration). 22/22 pytest assertions pass.

critical_code_review_comments: Object-storage init: init_storage() force-refreshes on any 404 from PUT/GET which handles session-key rotation cleanly. put_object/get_object propagate requests.HTTPError; the serve endpoint (GET /api/uploads/{filename}) catches only HTTPError -> 404 — a network-level error (ConnectionError/Timeout) would surface as a 500 to the client. Consider wrapping in a broader except requests.RequestException and returning 502/503 for clarity.

GET /api/uploads/{filename} accepts JWT via ?token= query-param so tags can render; this exposes the JWT in server access logs and referrer headers. Consider a short-lived signed download URL (HMAC of filename+exp) instead of piping the full JWT through query strings.
assert_same_school_or_superuser is called AFTER a 404-safe find_one, which correctly avoids leaking existence. Good.

write_audit() swallows all exceptions with a warning — that's the right choice for a best-effort side-effect, but audit-log persistence failures will be silent in production. If audit is a compliance requirement, add a metric/alarm counter for write_audit failures.

The 4 upload endpoints persist storage_path in db.uploads; if init_storage() is re-provisioned to a different bucket the old storage_path will 404. Serving code falls back to local disk only — there is no re-mapping if the storage backend key namespace changes. Document this operational constraint or store the STORAGE_URL base alongside storage_path for future migration.
forgot_password uses uuid.uuid4().hex as the reset token (128 bits). Fine, but consider secrets.token_urlsafe(32) which is slightly stronger and unambiguously random.

Non-blocking: audit rows are indexed by created_at desc but there is no compound index on (school_code, entity_type, entity_id). At scale the audit-logs GET with entity_id filter will full-scan per tenant.
